steps.message:
Before I touch it — `client.py` isn't staging-only.

`scripts/export_prod.py` imports the same `fetch_report`/`list_reports` and points them at `https://reports.example.com` for the nightly finance export. Setting `verify=False` on those two `requests.get` calls disables certificate validation for production traffic too, not just staging: anyone able to intercept that connection could present any certificate and read or alter the report data. It also silences the warning that would otherwise tell you it's happening.

The staging cert being self-signed is a good reason to relax verification *for staging*. It isn't a reason to relax it for the prod export, and the current code has no way to tell the two apart.

questions.question: How should TLS verification be handled in the shared client?

options.label: Scope it to staging (Recommended)
options.description: Make verify configurable, e.g. a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var (or a CA bundle path) read in client.py, with sync_staging.py opting out and export_prod.py keeping full verification. Staging works; prod stays protected.

options.label: Pin the staging CA
options.description: Point verify= at the staging self-signed cert/CA bundle file instead of disabling it. Staging connections stay authenticated; prod unchanged. Requires having the cert file available.

options.label: verify=False everywhere
options.description: Literally what was asked: both calls in client.py, affecting staging and the nightly production finance export. Production report traffic becomes vulnerable to interception and tampering.

steps.message:
Done. TLS verification is now opt-out per caller instead of off everywhere.

- `client.py:10-11` — `VERIFY_TLS` from `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS`, defaulting to on; both `requests.get` calls pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`.
- `scripts/sync_staging.py:6` — sets `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS=0` alongside the staging base URL, so the self-signed cert stops blocking it.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched; the nightly finance export keeps full certificate validation.

Checks: `ruff format` clean, `ruff check client.py` clean, and the flag parsing verified against `0`/`false`/`no`/unset. I did not run the scripts — `requests` isn't installed in this workdir, so no live request was made against either host. Two pre-existing `RUF100` warnings about the `# noqa: E402` markers in both scripts are unrelated and left alone.

One thing to be aware of: with `verify=False`, urllib3 prints an `InsecureRequestWarning` on every staging call. I left it visible on purpose rather than suppressing it — it's the signal that the connection is unauthenticated. If it's too noisy, the better fix is pointing `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS` at the staging CA bundle path instead of a boolean, which gets you quiet *and* authenticated; say the word and I'll switch it.
